sylvan esso|hot slob.fact: Hot Slob is Sylvan Esso's first new single since 2022's No Rules Sandy, released in 2026 on their own label, Psychic Hotline. It features drummer TJ Maiani (Weyes Blood, Neneh Cherry) and Jenn Wasner of Wye Oak on extra guitar and vocals.

sylvan esso|concrete glen.fact: Concrete Glen, from Sylvan Esso's 2026 album Ow, samples Sigur Ros' "Svefn-g-englar" - a band singer Amelia Meath has said soundtracked a lot of her childhood.

king gizzard & the lizard wizard|crumbli.fact: Crumbling Castle's home album, Polygondwanaland, was released by King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard under an open license with the master tapes posted online for free - inviting fans and small labels to press and remix it however they liked. Hundreds of different fan-made editions exist, including a K.K. Slider-style Animal Crossing tribute pressed on vinyl.

r.e.m.|orange crush.fact: R.E.M.'s Orange Crush is a quietly anti-war song - the title nods to Agent Orange, the defoliant used in the Vietnam War, drawing on singer Michael Stipe's memories of growing up on Army bases where his father served. The subtlety worked almost too well: a British TV host once introduced it on air as "great on a summer's day."

bon iver|holocene.fact: Bon Iver's Holocene takes its title from both the current geological epoch and a bar in Portland, Oregon. Its three verses trace three different moments from Justin Vernon's life in his hometown of Eau Claire, Wisconsin, and the music video was filmed among Iceland's glaciers.

coldplay|don't panic.fact: Don't Panic was the very first song Coldplay ever played live, at their debut gig at The Laurel Tree in Camden, London, in January 1998 - two years before it appeared, reworked with a pump organ, on their debut album Parachutes.

the smiths|still ill.fact: The Smiths' Still Ill got its title from a real conversation - Morrissey's friend, artist Linder Sterling, greeted him at a weekly rooftop-restaurant meetup by asking, "Are you still ill?"

vampire weekend|run.fact: Vampire Weekend's Ezra Koenig has said Run, from 2010's Contra, was written with Bruce Springsteen's Born to Run in mind.

my morning jacket|i will sing you songs.fact: My Morning Jacket recorded It Still Moves, home to the nearly eight-minute I Will Sing You Songs, at Above the Cadillac Studios in rural Shelbyville, Kentucky - with the album's horn parts tracked separately at Memphis's famous Royal Studios.

the strokes|someday.fact: The melody for The Strokes' “Someday” reportedly came to Julian Casablancas while singing in the bathroom, nursing a hangover at drummer Fabrizio Moretti's house - the band built the song around what they heard him singing.

the decemberists|a beginning song.fact: The Decemberists closed their album What a Terrible World, What a Beautiful World with “A Beginning Song” - a hopeful, cathartic track meant to feel like something new being born out of the album's earlier, heavier songs.

alabama shakes|shoegaze.fact: Despite the name, Alabama Shakes' “Shoegaze” isn't about the genre - it's a song about restlessness and loneliness, pivoting on the line “It ain't no fun to be lonely.”

sigur ros|inni mer syngur vitleysingur.fact: Sigur Ros' Icelandic song title “Inní mér syngur vitleysingur” translates to “Within me a lunatic sings.” It's the second track on their 2008 album Með suð í eyrum við spilum endalaust.

tv on the radio|dlz.fact: TV on the Radio's “DLZ” stands for “Dawn of the Loser,” a phrase from the song's final lines. It wasn't released as a single, but got a big boost in popularity after appearing in a season 2 episode of Breaking Bad.

the cure|catch.fact: The Cure's “Catch” is a light, whimsical love song about a girl from Robert Smith's past whose name he can barely remember - a deliberate 180-degree turn from the album's more aggressive opening track.

kate bush|this woman's work.fact: Kate Bush wrote “This Woman's Work” for the 1988 film She's Having a Baby, matching her lyrics to a dramatic hospital scene the director had already sent her - it's sung from the perspective of a partner realizing how much he loves her.

sault|let me go.fact: SAULT is an anonymous British music collective that avoids media interviews entirely - even their exact lineup is unconfirmed, though producer Dean “Inflo” Josiah Cover (who's worked with Michael Kiwanuka and Little Simz) is rumored to be a member.

khruangbin|time (you and i).fact: Khruangbin's album Mordechai is named after a friend of bassist Laura Lee Ochoa who once encouraged her to jump off a waterfall - the feeling of that leap stuck with her, including on “Time (You and I),” a song about wishing you had more time with the people you love.

broadcast|valerie.fact: Broadcast's “Valerie” takes its name and melody from the 1970 Czech film Valerie and Her Week of Wonders, a major inspiration for the band's dreamy, psychedelic sound.

cherry glazerr|grilled cheese.fact: Cherry Glazerr's “Grilled Cheese” is exactly what it sounds like - a whimsical garage-pop song about grilled cheese sandwiches, written when the band members were still in high school.

boygenius|bite the hand.fact: boygenius wrote “Bite the Hand” about the strange etiquette of fame - not feeling obligated to give fans a piece of yourself just because they bought a ticket, while still making music that's honest.

beabadoobee|beaches.fact: beabadoobee's “Beaches” is a song about self-discovery and not waiting around for the right moment - “Don't wait for the tide, just to dip both your feet in” - built on crunchy guitars that recall Weezer's “Island in the Sun.”

anna burch|tea-soaked letter.fact: In the video for Anna Burch's “Tea-Soaked Letter,” she makes tea, makes toast, and reads tarot cards while waiting to hear from the person she's singing about - a song asking a love interest to actually follow through on better communication.

phoebe bridgers|bobby.fact: Phoebe Bridgers' “Bobby” is her most straightforward love song yet, widely believed to be about her partner Bo Burnham - a warm departure from the melancholic tone of her earlier album Punisher.

hum|why i like the robins.fact: Hum's “Why I Like the Robins” comes from You'd Prefer an Astronaut, an album full of space imagery - this song imagines watching from a window for the robins to return, and seeing the world through a loved one's eyes.

mary in the junkyard|myrtle.fact: Mary in the Junkyard's “Myrtle” is named for a comforting turtle character - “Myrtle told me that I don't need to worry” - part of a concept album imagining the singer's past life as a fisherman.

beach house|april suzanne.fact: Beach House's “April Suzanne” is a cover of a 1976 song by Robert Lester Folsom, released as a limited 7″ single (only 1,000 copies worldwide) to celebrate the 50th anniversary of his album Music and Dreams.

spoon|got nuffin.fact: Spoon's Britt Daniel described “Got Nuffin” as being about having “nothing to lose but darkness and shadows” - a song about the relief of shaking off negative thoughts.

hoodoo gurus|i want you back.fact: Hoodoo Gurus' “I Want You Back” sounds like a breakup song, but frontman Dave Faulkner wrote it about a former bandmate who quit and was dismissive on the way out - he flipped the anger into a mock “spurned lover” song aimed right at him.

hatchie|quicksand.fact: Hatchie's “Quicksand” catches her in a familiar cycle - feeling ungrateful even when things in her life are, on paper, going well.

weyes blood|movies.fact: Weyes Blood's “Movies” is an ode to cinema as a modern myth-maker - she wants her own life to have the meaning a movie does, even while admitting “the meaning of life doesn't seem to shine like that screen.”

m83|midnight city.fact: M83's “Midnight City” was inspired by late nights watching Downtown Los Angeles come alive, and ends with a now-iconic saxophone solo played by James King of Fitz and the Tantrums.

slow pulp|red car.fact: On Slow Pulp's “Red Car,” a 1996 Mazda becomes a stand-in for the possibility of starting over - part of their album Melodie, about feeling stuck and finding a way to move on.

mitski|first love / late spring.fact: Mitski has said “First Love / Late Spring” came from falling in love at a moment when she really couldn't afford to. The song describes crying like a “tall child” - looking like an adult while feeling as overwhelmed as a kid.

pavement|unseen power of the picket fenc.fact: Pavement wrote “The Unseen Power of the Picket Fence” as a loving, joke-filled tribute to R.E.M. for a 1994 charity compilation - Stephen Malkmus jokingly name-drops their songs and admits “Time After Time” was his least favorite, which reportedly needled Michael Stipe a little.

the sundays|life goes on.fact: The Sundays' “Life Goes On” opens with “Build me up don't get me down, weather the storm, well, life goes on” - a simple, steady message of resilience from their final album, Static & Silence.

kurt vile|99 bpm.fact: Kurt Vile's “99 BPM” is a nostalgic nod to playing in bands with a friend named Rob back around 2012 - “99 BPM, well, what's that between friends?”

black midi|hogwash and balderdash.fact: black midi's “Hogwash and Balderdash” tells the story of two runaway convicts on the run from the law - who happen to be chickens named Hogwash and Balderdash.

ween|learnin' to love.fact: Ween's “Learnin' to Love” came together after Gene Ween stumbled on a website full of horse-racing betting slang and turned it into a song.

sports team|i'm in love (subaru).fact: Sports Team's “I'm In Love (Subaru)” is a love song about a shiny red Subaru - a stand-in for an idealized, “sorted” adult life that, the song admits, can't actually be bought.

dazy|beat change.fact: Dazy is the one-man project of James Goodson, who started anonymously posting songs on Bandcamp during the pandemic summer of 2020 before it grew into a full band.

talking heads|memories can't wait.fact: David Byrne described Talking Heads' “Memories Can't Wait” as the band's version of a metal song - about memories that keep flooding back no matter how much you try to move on.

vampire weekend|obvious bicycle.fact: Vampire Weekend's “Obvious Bicycle” never actually says the words “obvious” or “bicycle” anywhere in the lyrics - it was just the title Rostam Batmanglij gave the demo the day he wrote it, and it stuck.

angel olsen|all mirrors.fact: Angel Olsen has said “All Mirrors” grew from the idea that “we are all mirrors to and for each other” - a song about how people and memories keep echoing each other over time.

francis of delirium|it's a beautiful lif.fact: Francis of Delirium built “It's a Beautiful Life” out of small real moments - coffee with a pianist about to play a Philip Glass piece, and watching a choir rehearse in a basement - finding beauty alongside everyday loneliness.

swapmeet|bonny.fact: Swapmeet's “Bonny” includes a shoutout to the TV show Malcolm in the Middle - the band has said it made the cut mainly because it fit the syllable count of the line.

future islands|the tower.fact: Future Islands' “The Tower” takes its name and theme from W.B. Yeats' 1928 poem of the same name, about aging and the passage of time, built around the image of a lighthouse cutting through darkness.

bon iver|heavenly father - mediolanum, m.fact: Bon Iver's Justin Vernon wrote “Heavenly Father” for Zach Braff's film Wish I Was Here after talking with his own brother about the film's story of two brothers - it became a song about searching for peace.

black marble|it always comes to me.fact: Black Marble's “It Always Comes to Me” sketches a character who always seems to get away with things, charm or deceit - a modern cousin of The Kinks' “Dedicated Follower of Fashion.”

sharp pins|it's a mod mod world.fact: Sharp Pins is the lo-fi pop project of Chicago musician Kai Slater (also of the band Lifeguard) - “It's a Mod Mod World” is deliberately recorded to sound like catching a British Invasion hit on a handheld AM radio in the 1960s.
